name: PostgreSQL
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in PostgreSQL as a competency should be able to deeply understand and reason about PostgreSQL architecture (process model, MVCC, WAL, shared buffers, checkpoints, catalog, storage layout), expertly design and optimize schemas (normalization, denormalization, data types, constraints, referential integrity, multi-tenancy, schema evolution), write and tune complex SQL (joins, CTEs, window functions, advanced aggregation, JSON/JSONB, range types, DML/DDL, anti-pattern avoidance), master indexing (B-tree, GiST, GIN, BRIN, partial/expression indexes, index bloat, full-text, geospatial, statistics), analyze and optimize query plans (EXPLAIN, join strategies, planner tuning, bulk operations, N+1, CTE materialization, monitoring, benchmarking), manage transactions and concurrency (isolation levels, locking, deadlocks, advisory locks, long transactions, connection pooling), handle large-scale storage and partitioning (TOAST, declarative partitioning, tablespaces, bloat, archival, time-series), leverage advanced features (JSONB, full-text, arrays, range types, exclusion constraints, materialized views, triggers, NOTIFY/LISTEN, RLS, multi-tenancy, new features), architect high availability and replication (streaming replication, logical replication, failover, replica lag, HA topologies, orchestration tools), implement robust backup and disaster recovery (pg_dump, pg_basebackup, PITR, backup policies, restore drills, configuration backup, DR automation), enforce security and compliance (roles, pg_hba.conf, TLS, auditing, RLS, password policies, encryption, compliance standards), use and manage extensions and procedural languages (pg_stat_statements, PostGIS, PL/pgSQL, FDW, background workers, extension lifecycle), automate and operate PostgreSQL (autovacuum, monitoring, alerting, incident response, capacity planning, OS tuning, upgrades, migrations, CI/CD integration), and collaborate effectively (documentation, governance, mentoring, cross-team communication, release tracking, inventory management).
long_scope:
{"sections":[{"name":"Core PostgreSQL Architecture & Fundamentals","scope_included":"- Understand PostgreSQL’s overall architecture and process model (postmaster, backend processes, background workers) and how that impacts performance, isolation, and reliability.
- Understand MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) deeply: tuple versions, visibility rules, hint bits, transaction IDs, and how these underpin isolation and concurrency.
- Know how WAL (Write-Ahead Log) works conceptually: WAL records, durability guarantees, fsync, full_page_writes, and how WAL volume affects IO and replication.
- Understand shared buffers, OS page cache, work_mem, temp files, and how PostgreSQL uses memory and disk for query execution.
- Understand checkpointing: what a checkpoint does, how checkpoint frequency and size affect performance and recovery time, and how to tune related parameters.
- Be able to reason about how configuration parameters map to underlying hardware resources (CPU, RAM, storage, network) for OLTP and OLAP workloads.
- Understand how VACUUM and autovacuum relate to MVCC and bloat, and the tradeoffs between aggressive and conservative vacuum settings.
- Understand the catalog structure conceptually (pg_class, pg_attribute, pg_type, pg_index, etc.) and how PostgreSQL stores metadata.
- Know the implications of different storage parameters (fillfactor, toast, autovacuum_* options per table) and how they affect performance and bloat.
- Understand when and why to use different encoding, collation, and locale options and their implications for sorting, indexing, and comparisons.
- Understand transaction log and data directory layout at a conceptual level (base, global, pg_wal, pg_tblspc, pg_stat, pg_stat_tmp) and what each is used for.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"SQL Proficiency & Advanced Querying","scope_included":"- Be fluent in writing complex SELECT queries, including multi-join queries, subqueries, CTEs (WITH queries), and nested expressions with correct semantics and performance implications.
- Use window functions extensively (partitioning, ordering, framing options, aggregates vs window functions) for analytics and reporting queries.
- Leverage advanced aggregation patterns (GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, CUBE) for multidimensional reporting where appropriate.
- Use advanced filtering and search constructs (IN, EXISTS/NOT EXISTS, scalar and correlated subqueries) with an understanding of performance tradeoffs.
- Use PostgreSQL-specific SQL features: DISTINCT ON, RETURNING clauses, UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT), and lateral joins (LATERAL) appropriately.
- Apply JSON/JSONB operations in SQL (->, ->>, #>, #>>, @>, ? operators, jsonb_set, jsonb_agg, jsonb_build_object, etc.) with consideration for index usage.
- Use range types and operators where suitable (int4range, tstzrange, etc.) and understand how GiST/GiN indexes can accelerate them.
- Understand when and how to use temporary tables, unlogged tables, and materialized views, and the tradeoffs in performance and durability.
- Compose DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) that scales for bulk operations, including batching strategies, COPY usage, and minimizing row-by-row processing.
- Write robust DDL that manages dependencies correctly (foreign keys, constraints, indexes, triggers, views, materialized views) without breaking existing consumers.
- Ensure SQL is written with explicit handling of NULL semantics, data type casting, and collation-aware comparisons to avoid subtle correctness issues.
- Understand anti-patterns such as overusing SELECT *, using functions in WHERE clauses that defeat index usage, and relying on implicit casts that hurt performance.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Modeling, Schema Design & Constraints","scope_included":"- Design normalized schemas (up to at least 3NF) and know when and how to selectively denormalize for performance or reporting.
- Choose appropriate data types for each column (including numeric vs integer vs bigint, timestamp vs timestamptz, text vs varchar, enums, ranges, JSON/JSONB, arrays) based on correctness and performance.
- Use constraints effectively: PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY, and exclusion constraints, understanding how they are enforced and indexed.
- Design referential integrity using foreign keys, including ON DELETE/UPDATE rules (CASCADE, SET NULL, RESTRICT) and their effect on application behavior.
- Understand and use identity/serial columns (SERIAL vs GENERATED ALWAYS/GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY) and implications for dumps and restores.
- Model one-to-many, many-to-many, and polymorphic relationships effectively using junction tables or appropriate patterns.
- Design schemas suitable for multi-tenant deployments (schema-per-tenant, row-based tenant isolation, database-per-tenant) and understand tradeoffs.
- Make informed use of PostgreSQL-specific modeling features such as arrays, composite types, and JSONB for semi-structured data.
- Apply naming conventions, schema organization (public vs dedicated schemas), and separation of concerns for application, reporting, and admin objects.
- Evaluate and refactor existing schemas for performance and maintainability: detecting unnecessary columns, redundant indexes, or mis-modeled relationships.
- Use domain types for enforcing reusable business rules and constraints when appropriate.
- Understand and plan for future schema evolution to minimize downtime and risk (backwards-compatible changes, rolling deployments).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Indexing Strategies & Internals","scope_included":"- Understand internal behavior of B-tree indexes (structure, page splits, index-only scans, correlation) and their performance characteristics.
- Choose between index types (B-tree, Hash, GiST, GIN, BRIN, SP-GiST, bloom) based on data distribution and query patterns.
- Design composite (multi-column) indexes with correct column ordering based on filters, joins, and sorting requirements.
- Use partial indexes and understand how predicates influence planner choice and index size.
- Use expression indexes (e.g., lower(col), JSONB expressions) and know when they are necessary to support frequently used computed predicates.
- Understand index maintenance costs (write overhead, vacuum impact, bloat) and balance index count with performance.
- Diagnose index bloat and use appropriate remediation (REINDEX, REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, pg_repack, index recreation in rolling fashion).
- Interpret index usage statistics (pg_stat_user_indexes, pg_stat_io, pg_statio_user_indexes) to validate that important indexes are being used.
- Understand when index-only scans are possible and how visibility map affects them.
- Know how to design indexes for advanced use cases: full-text search (tsvector/tsquery, GIN/GiST), similarity search (pg_trgm), range queries, and geospatial queries (PostGIS).
- Avoid common indexing anti-patterns (creating redundant overlapping indexes, indexing low-selectivity columns that don’t help, over-indexing write-heavy tables).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Query Planning, Optimization & Performance Tuning","scope_included":"- Interpret EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output in depth, including node types (Seq Scan, Index Scan, Index Only Scan, Bitmap Heap/Index Scan, Hash Join, Merge Join, Nested Loop, etc.), row estimates, actual rows, and timing.
- Identify misestimation issues (row count, selectivity) and correct them using ANALYZE, extended statistics (ndistinct, MCV lists), and query rewrites.
- Optimize joins: choosing correct join types, join order, and ensuring indexes support join predicates.
- Tune queries for both OLTP and OLAP scenarios, recognizing when to favor many small queries vs fewer heavy analytical queries.
- Use planner configuration parameters judiciously (enable_nestloop, enable_seqscan, enable_hashjoin, etc.) for special-case troubleshooting without globally harming performance.
- Detect and resolve performance problems caused by sort and hash operations spilling to disk (work_mem tuning, query refactoring).
- Analyze and optimize queries using CTEs vs subqueries vs inline views, understanding PostgreSQL’s CTE materialization behavior and changes in newer versions.
- Use statement-level monitoring (pg_stat_statements or similar) to identify top queries by time, frequency, and resource usage, then systematically tune them.
- Recognize N+1 query patterns and other inefficient application-side query patterns and propose DB-centric solutions (set-based operations, caching, batching).
- Optimize bulk loading and batch processing jobs using COPY, unlogged tables, disabled constraints/indexes where safe, and staged loading techniques.
- Apply and verify performance fixes through controlled benchmarking, baseline metrics, and regression detection.
- Understand how autovacuum and vacuum settings impact query performance and plan changes appropriately (e.g., dealing with dead tuples and bloat).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Transactions, Concurrency & Locking","scope_included":"- Understand transaction lifecycles, including BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK semantics, subtransactions, and savepoints.
- Use PostgreSQL isolation levels (READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE) appropriately based on business requirements and concurrency tradeoffs.
- Diagnose and handle anomalies (phantoms, non-repeatable reads) and know when higher isolation is required.
- Understand row-level locking behavior (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT) and design queries to avoid lock contention.
- Interpret and resolve blocking and deadlocks by using views like pg_locks, pg_stat_activity, and log analysis.
- Understand how DDL locks work and plan schema changes to minimize downtime and contention (concurrent index builds, non-blocking migrations where possible).
- Explain and manage lock escalation patterns (e.g., relation locks, page locks in specific operations) and their impact on concurrent workloads.
- Design application logic that uses transactions correctly: idempotent operations, retry strategies for serialization failures or deadlocks.
- Understand long-running transactions’ impact on vacuum and bloat; design processes to avoid or mitigate them.
- Coordinate with application code to ensure connection pooling and transaction scoping do not create excessive idle-in-transaction sessions.
- Use advisory locks appropriately for application-level coordination, with clear strategies to avoid deadlock and orphaned locks.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Storage, Partitioning & Large-Scale Data Management","scope_included":"- Understand table storage formats, TOAST behavior for large values, and how that affects performance and index usage.
- Design and implement table partitioning using declarative partitioning (range, list, hash) and understand partition pruning behavior.
- Decide when partitioning is appropriate vs when it adds unnecessary complexity; size partitions sensibly and manage long-term data lifecycle (attach/detach/drop partitions).
- Understand how global vs local indexes and constraints behave with partitioned tables and how to design indexes for partitioned workloads.
- Manage large tables effectively: vacuum strategy, autovacuum tuning at table level, and periodic maintenance to control bloat.
- Evaluate and use tablespaces for storage layout when necessary, including separating hot vs cold data across disks.
- Handle bulk archival and purge operations in a way that avoids massive vacuum overhead and lock contention.
- Be aware of and manage the impact of bloated tables and indexes on disk usage, backup size, and performance.
- Understand the tradeoffs of unlogged tables and temporary tables for large transient datasets.
- Work with time-series or event data patterns efficiently, using partitioning, retention strategies, and write-optimized schema design.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Advanced PostgreSQL Features & Data Types","scope_included":"- Use JSON/JSONB extensively for semi-structured data, including complex queries, indexing strategies (GIN with jsonb_ops/jsonb_path_ops), and validation patterns.
- Use full-text search capabilities: tsvector, tsquery, dictionaries, stemming, ranking, and combined queries with other filters.
- Work with array types effectively (array operations, unnest, containment operators) and know when arrays are vs are not appropriate modeling tools.
- Use range types and exclusion constraints for time/interval scheduling, resource booking, and non-overlapping intervals.
- Understand and use generated columns where appropriate for derived values that need to be indexed.
- Use materialized views for precomputed heavy queries, with a refresh strategy (REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY) that aligns with SLAs.
- Implement triggers and rules responsibly, preferring triggers for data integrity or audit needs and avoiding business logic that belongs in the application layer.
- Use advisory locks, NOTIFY/LISTEN, and other built-in primitives for inter-process coordination and event-driven patterns.
- Leverage configuration and features for multi-tenancy and security isolation (RLS, separate schemas or databases) when required.
- Be aware of newer PostgreSQL features across recent versions and make informed decisions on adopting them (e.g., improvements to partitioning, parallelism, JIT, logical replication, etc.).","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"High Availability, Replication & Failover","scope_included":"- Configure and operate streaming replication (physical replication) with one or more standbys, including synchronous vs asynchronous modes and tradeoffs.
- Understand replication slots, their purpose, and risks (e.g., disk growth if replicas fall behind) and monitor them appropriately.
- Design replication topologies suitable for the organization (primary-standby, cascading replication, read replicas for reporting).
- Configure and test automatic or semi-automatic failover using tooling such as Patroni, repmgr, or other orchestration solutions.
- Understand timeline management, promotion of standbys, and failover behavior, including split-brain risks and how to mitigate them.
- Use logical replication for selective table replication or versioned upgrades, understanding its limitations (sequence handling, DDL replication, etc.).
- Plan for and handle replica lag: monitoring, tuning parameters (wal_level, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots), and application strategies for stale reads.
- Utilize hot standbys for read scaling, with awareness of Hot Standby conflicts and how to handle them (max_standby_* settings, query cancellation strategies).
- Understand replication performance factors: network latency, WAL volume, compression, synchronous_commit settings, and their impact on throughput and durability.
- Participate in designing HA strategies that include load balancers, VIPs, or DNS failover, and understand end-to-end behavior during failover events.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Backup, Restore & Disaster Recovery","scope_included":"- Configure and operate logical backups using pg_dump/pg_restore, including parallel options and strategies for large databases.
- Manage physical backups using pg_basebackup or third-party tools (e.g., pgBackRest, WAL-G) and understand base backup plus WAL archiving patterns.
- Design and implement backup policies that meet RPO/RTO requirements, including backup frequency, retention, and storage considerations.
- Perform and validate Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR), including creating restore plans, configuring recovery parameters, and testing restores regularly.
- Understand the differences, tradeoffs, and appropriate use cases for logical vs physical backups.
- Be able to restore backups to new hardware or environments (test, staging) for both recovery drills and cloning workflows.
- Ensure backups include critical configuration and cluster-wide data (e.g., pg_hba.conf, postgresql.conf, custom config, replication slots where appropriate).
- Assess and minimize backup window and impact on production workloads, using throttling or offloading to replicas when possible.
- Document and regularly test DR procedures, ensuring they are automated and repeatable where possible.
- Monitor backup integrity, completeness, and failure alerts, and respond effectively to backup or restore failures.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Security, Auditing & Compliance","scope_included":"- Design and manage roles, privileges, and grant hierarchies using roles, groups, and database/schema/table-level permissions.
- Implement secure authentication methods (password, SCRAM, SSL client certs, Kerberos/LDAP/OAuth integration via middleware) aligned with organizational policies.
- Configure pg_hba.conf securely, limiting access by IP, role, and authentication type, and regularly reviewing for least privilege.
- Implement TLS encryption for client connections, manage certificates, and understand how to verify secure connections from clients.
- Apply row-level security (RLS) policies for multi-tenant or sensitive data scenarios and validate policy correctness and performance.
- Understand and configure password policies (complexity, rotation), connection limits, and role attributes (LOGIN, SUPERUSER, REPLICATION, BYPASSRLS) safely.
- Set up and interpret logging for security-relevant events (failed logins, permission errors, DDL changes, privilege escalations).
- Use or integrate auditing tools/extensions (e.g., pgaudit or similar) when detailed auditing is required for compliance.
- Understand data masking, anonymization, and encryption-at-rest strategies (filesystem/disk-level encryption, KMS integration) and how PostgreSQL fits into them.
- Collaborate with security/compliance teams to ensure PostgreSQL configuration aligns with standards such as SOC2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or internal guidelines.
- Periodically review schema and permissions for privilege creep, unused superuser accounts, and insecure defaults.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Extensions, Procedural Languages & Ecosystem Integration","scope_included":"- Evaluate and use common extensions such as pg_stat_statements, pg_trgm, btree_gin, hstore, uuid-ossp, citext, and PostGIS as needed.
- Understand extension installation, versioning, and upgrade processes, and manage them across environments.
- Write and maintain PL/pgSQL functions, triggers, and stored procedures with good performance and error handling.
- Be familiar with adding other procedural languages (PL/Python, PL/Perl, PL/V8, etc.) and understand security and performance considerations.
- Use background worker–based extensions or logical decoding plugins where advanced functionality is needed, understanding their operational overhead.
- Integrate PostgreSQL with external systems: FDWs (postgres_fdw, file_fdw, or others) for querying external sources, understanding performance and consistency characteristics.
- Ensure that use of extensions does not compromise portability or upgradeability without a conscious architectural decision.
- Understand the support and maturity characteristics of community vs vendor extensions and how that influences adoption.
- Leverage pg_stat_* views and contrib extensions to gain deeper operational insights and drive optimization or capacity decisions.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Maintenance, Monitoring & Operations","scope_included":"- Configure and tune autovacuum at cluster and table level, including thresholds and scaling, based on workload and bloat patterns.
- Plan and run manual VACUUM (including VACUUM FULL where appropriate) and ANALYZE operations safely and with minimal impact on availability.
- Monitor core health metrics: connections, CPU, memory, IO, WAL rate, bloat, replication lag, query latency, and throughput.
- Use built-in statistics views (pg_stat_activity, pg_stat_database, pg_stat_all_tables, pg_stat_user_indexes, pg_statio_*, pg_stat_statements) for ongoing monitoring and troubleshooting.
- Interpret logs (with appropriate log_line_prefix and log settings) to detect slow queries, lock waits, autovacuum behavior, and errors.
- Participate in capacity planning: disk space projections, growth estimates, memory and CPU sizing, and connection pool requirements.
- Develop and implement maintenance windows and routines (index maintenance, vacuum tuning, reindexing strategies, statistics refresh, partition maintenance).
- Design and monitor alerting thresholds that distinguish between transient and critical issues, reducing alert fatigue.
- Prepare for and handle common operational incidents: connection storms, autovacuum thrashing, runaway queries, bloat spikes, and disk filling due to WAL or temp files.
- Keep PostgreSQL versions reasonably current, understanding deprecation timelines and security patching cadence from the PostgreSQL community or vendor.
- Understand basic storage characteristics (latency, throughput, IOPS limits, burst behavior) and their relationship with PostgreSQL performance.
- Coordinate with infrastructure teams on OS tuning (kernel parameters, huge pages, swappiness, transparent huge pages, filesystem choices) that affect PostgreSQL.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Migrations, Upgrades & Cross-Environment Management","scope_included":"- Plan and execute major version upgrades (pg_upgrade, logical replication–based migration, dump/restore) with controlled downtime and rollback strategies.
- Understand behavior changes and compatibility concerns between major PostgreSQL versions and how to account for them during upgrades.
- Manage schema migrations using tools (e.g., Flyway, Liquibase, Rails migrations, Django migrations, or similar) and integrate them into CI/CD pipelines.
- Design migration steps to be backwards-compatible where possible (online schema changes, rolling deployments) to minimize disruption.
- Handle data transformations at scale during migrations, including backfilling, re-indexing, and phased rollouts.
- Manage multiple environments (dev, test, staging, production) with consistent schema, configuration, and data subsets for testing.
- Coordinate application and database changes to avoid race conditions or inconsistent behavior during deployments.
- Validate migrations and upgrades through rehearsals in staging environments and storing runbooks capturing each step.
- Plan for decommissioning legacy databases, including data archival, access to historical data, and compliance requirements.
- Resolve migration-related issues such as long-running locks, large table alterations, and performance regressions after version changes.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Scripting, Automation & Application Integration","scope_included":"- Automate routine database tasks (backups, vacuums, statistics refreshes, partition management, health checks) using scripts or orchestration tools.
- Use psql and other command-line tools effectively in scripts, including safe handling of credentials and error checking.
- Integrate PostgreSQL efficiently with common application frameworks and ORMs, influencing query generation and connection behavior as needed.
- Design and enforce connection management strategies, including proper use of connection pooling (PgBouncer/pgpool or language-specific pools) and sensible pool sizing.
- Write stored procedures and SQL/PL scripts that encapsulate complex data operations for performance or consistency, while balancing maintainability.
- Implement data export/import workflows between PostgreSQL and other systems (data warehouses, queues, caches) using COPY, FDWs, or ETL tools.
- Use APIs and drivers (JDBC, psycopg, libpq, etc.) with an understanding of parameter binding, prepared statements, and transaction scope.
- Integrate PostgreSQL monitoring data into centralized observability systems (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, etc.) via exporters and log shipping.
- Ensure automation is idempotent, safe to rerun, and thoroughly tested to reduce operational risk.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Tooling, Setup & Environment Management","scope_included":"- Install and configure PostgreSQL on common platforms (Linux distributions, containers, cloud-managed instances) following best practices for directories, permissions, and basic security.
- Configure key parameters in postgresql.conf and related files based on workload patterns (shared_buffers, work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, effective_cache_size, autovacuum_*, checkpoint_*, wal_level, max_connections, etc.).
- Use administrative tools and GUIs (psql, pgAdmin, DBeaver, or equivalents) effectively for management and troubleshooting.
- Work with connection poolers (PgBouncer, pgpool-II, or managed equivalents) and understand pool modes, timeouts, and failure behavior.
- Operate PostgreSQL in containerized or orchestrated environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and understand persistent storage and configuration management there.
- Use configuration management tools (Ansible, Chef, Puppet, Terraform, Helm, etc.) to maintain consistent PostgreSQL setups across environments.
- Understand managed PostgreSQL offerings (AWS RDS/Aurora, GCP Cloud SQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, etc.) and their configuration constraints vs self-managed clusters.
- Manage OS-level settings and integration (systemd service configuration, log rotation, file descriptors, kernel SHMMAX/SHMALL limits) relevant to PostgreSQL.
- Maintain and version-control configuration files and initialization scripts, ensuring reproducible environment setup.
- Participate in hardware and infrastructure selection discussions, advising on storage types (SSD/NVMe vs HDD), RAID, and network requirements from the database perspective.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Testing, Quality Assurance & Troubleshooting Practices","scope_included":"- Design and perform load and stress tests that model real workloads against PostgreSQL, using appropriate tools and realistic data.
- Build database-level tests (e.g., unit tests for functions, integration tests for complex queries and constraints) within the broader testing strategy.
- Use staging environments with production-like data volumes to validate performance changes, migrations, and major configuration adjustments.
- Develop structured troubleshooting approaches: systematically isolating whether performance regressions are due to queries, schema, configuration, hardware, or external factors.
- Capture and analyze diagnostics for complex problems: auto_explain, log_min_duration_statement, statement statistics, and OS-level metrics.
- Identify common failure modes (out-of-disk for WAL or data, connection storms, vacuum freeze thresholds, corrupted indexes) and execute remediation steps.
- Assess and optimize query patterns generated by ORMs and other frameworks, introducing database-side optimization or guidance as necessary.
- Collaborate with developers and SREs to ensure performance and reliability regressions are detected early through automated checks and dashboards.
- Maintain runbooks for recurring issues and ensure lessons learned are codified into configuration changes, alerts, or tooling improvements.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Collaboration, Governance & Documentation","scope_included":"- Document database schemas, key tables, relationships, and business rules (constraints, triggers, RLS policies) in a form accessible to developers and stakeholders.
- Maintain documentation of critical operational procedures: backup/restore, failover, DR drills, upgrade/migration runbooks, and maintenance procedures.
- Communicate database constraints and capabilities clearly to application teams, influencing design decisions to align with PostgreSQL strengths.
- Participate in architecture and design reviews, providing PostgreSQL-focused input on data modeling, transaction boundaries, and scaling strategies.
- Establish and enforce coding and SQL style guidelines, review database-related code (migrations, functions, queries) for quality and performance.
- Provide mentoring and knowledge sharing to less experienced engineers on PostgreSQL fundamentals, best practices, and troubleshooting skills.
- Collaborate with security, compliance, and infrastructure teams to align PostgreSQL usage with organizational standards and regulatory requirements.
- Track and disseminate relevant changes from new PostgreSQL releases, advising when and how to adopt new features.
- Maintain an inventory of PostgreSQL instances, versions, critical configurations, and extension usage for governance and audit needs.","is_non_core_section":true}]}
